title.narrative: Continued Response to War in Ukraine 2024-2025 (EA11-2024)

description.narrative:
Now in its third year, the war in Ukraine continues to drive high levels of humanitarian needs, with the effects of fighting and its impact on infrastructure, livelihoods and access to services felt by displaced, returnee and non-displaced individuals across the country. The effects of the war are particularly strong in regions of the country closest to the frontlines and the Russian-Ukrainian border. Overall, OCHA estimated 14.6 million people living in Ukraine will require humanitarian assistance in 2024. Vulnerable war-affected households in Ukraine continue to face challenges in meeting their basic needs, primarily as a result of the depletion of resources and lack of income.
CSU will focus the proposed project on the oblasts of Ukraine with the greatest scale and severity of needs: Sumska, Kharkivska, Donetska, Dnipropetrovska, Zaporizhzhska, and Khersonska. Across the six oblasts, CSU will engage eight local centers in project implementation. CSU has chosen centers based on their ability to provide assistance to highly vulnerable displaced and returnee households, and to operate mobile teams that can provide assistance in rural areas, including in areas within 40 km or less of the frontline or Ukrainian-Russian border. This geographic targeting aligns with the priorities laid out in the OCHA Humanitarian Response Plan for 2024. 60 This project the response will prioritizes local centers that do not currently have emergency funding and those where the gap between funding and needs are high.
UKR020/1/2 will see CAFOD fund the positions of Grants Manager and National MEAL Manager for 12 months each as part of our organisational development contribution to Caritas SPES.
